title: main.record
description: record parses assure record (ST-ASR-CLI01). main in cmd/assure/main.go dispatches the first argument to it; the proof-run workflow runs it as go run -C cmd/assure -mod=readonly . record, so a relative path in a flag is read from cmd/assure, not from the root of the checkout: give each path absolute. It parses --commit, --go-json (the go test -json output), --python-json (the output of scripts/run-python-tests.py) and --predicate with the flag package, and exits 2 when one is missing or another argument is given. recordProofRun reads the job identity from the GitHub Actions environment (ReadGitHubRun: provider, run reference, signer, whether the workflow is the trusted signer), the root of the git repository that holds the working folder, the state of the checkout (ReadCheckout, which also sees changes that git status hides), and the spec from the git objects of the commit checked out (ReadCommittedSpec), never from the working tree. RecordProofRun builds the proof run and writes the predicate through GitHubAttestations to the absolute predicate path, for the attest job to sign with actions/attest. It exits 1 and writes nothing when RecordProofRun refuses.

title: main.gate
description: gate reads the subcommand: gateChangeCommand parses assure gate change (ST-ASR-CLI02) and gateReleaseCommand parses assure gate release (ST-ASR-CLI03), each with the flag package. Run with go run -C cmd/assure, a relative path in a flag is read from cmd/assure, not from the root of the checkout: give each path absolute; the change gate job builds assure from the base commit, and the gate-release job builds it from the release commit, and each runs that binary. Both read the git repository that holds the working folder and the commits from its git objects, never from the working tree; the Lathe CLI is node_modules/.bin/lathe of the repository unless --lathe names another, and the gate jobs name the Lathe they build. ReadGitHubGate reads the trusted signer, the change ref (GITHUB_REF, which it reads for both gates and only the change gate uses), the API (GITHUB_API_URL), the repository slug and the token (GITHUB_TOKEN) from the job environment. gitHubProvider opens GitHub's attestation store through the REST API with the token, and checks each Sigstore bundle in process against the public-good trust root, which TUF fetches into a new folder under RUNNER_TEMP, or the system's temporary folder when RUNNER_TEMP is not set, that it removes when done. The decision with every reason goes to stdout and is appended to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. gateRelease also reads the job's own workflow identity (ReadGitHubRun) as the signer of a passed decision, and before it gates, JobOutput.Check refuses a step summary or a predicate inside the repository and a predicate file that is already there, which it does not remove. After a refused release it prints ::notice::release refused: N reasons for the CI log and exits 1, and the gate-release job ends green. It writes the decision predicate for the attest-release job to sign only when the release passes. On exit 2, keepNoDecision writes one line to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, when the summary is outside the repository, that says no decision was reached and why; when the predicate of a passed decision cannot be written, that line follows the decision.

title: main.ledger
description: ledger parses assure ledger (ST-ASR-CLI04) with the flag package: --commit, and --depth (DefaultLedgerDepth, 200). buildLedger reads the trusted signer, the API and the token from the environment (ReadGitHubGate), but no change ref and no base; it opens GitHub's attestation store through gitHubProvider and builds the ledger with BuildLedger from verified attestations and the spec in the git objects of the repository that holds the working folder, walking first-parent history. It runs no Lathe. ledgerText prints the ledger; NotPassedAt gives the test records that did not pass. It exits 2 with no ledger when the flags are wrong or BuildLedger fails.

title: main.runDependencies
description: runDependencies parses stego deps (ST-BLD-CLI01) with the flag package and refuses any argument. It builds the reconciler input from the working folder (buildReconcilerInput: the resolved registry, STEGO_MODULE and STEGO_GO_VERSION) and calls compiler.ResolveDependencies, which runs Go's module tools and writes go.mod and go.sum, under a context that an interrupt cancels.

title: main.runBuild
description: runBuild parses stego build download (ST-BLD-CLI02), stego build (ST-BLD-CLI03), stego build verify (ST-BLD-CLI07) and stego build verify-source (ST-BLD-CLI08) by the first argument, each with its own flag set. download fills appbuild.DownloadOptions and calls appbuild.Download; the bare build fills appbuild.Options, with --go as bin/go of the selected official SDK (not from the archetype), and calls appbuild.Build, then prints the Application built event that appbuild.ApplicationBuiltIn reads from the result folder; both run under a context that SIGINT or SIGTERM cancels, and --source is a Git repository. verify calls appbuild.Verify and verify-source calls appbuild.VerifySource, which reads a snapshot with no Git metadata. --module-cache is optional: without it, appbuild.Build downloads modules through the module proxy with the network on. Each refuses a positional argument and a missing required flag. Not written yet: appbuild.Build writes application, build.json and SHA256SUMS into the result folder, and no SBOM, though stego build (ST-BLD-CLI03) says it writes both SBOMs.

title: main.runImage
description: runImage parses stego image build (ST-BLD-CLI04), hands stego image sign (ST-BLD-CLI05) to runImageSign, stego image publish (ST-BLD-CLI06), stego image retrieve (ST-BLD-CLI10) and stego image verify (ST-BLD-CLI09) by the first argument, each with its own flag set, under a context that SIGINT or SIGTERM cancels and a five-minute time limit. build fills appbuild.ImageOptions (an explicit PEM CA bundle as --trust-store) and calls appbuild.BuildImage, which writes an OCI image on scratch; with --after and --build-result it reads the Application built event with readEvent and calls appbuild.BuildImageOnApplicationBuilt (ST-BLD-PO01-H) instead. Either way it prints the Image built event with printEvent. publish and retrieve share appbuild.RegistryImageOptions: --record and --record-sha256 (the image record, which registryImage reads first with readTrustedImageRecord), --build-record, --work, the registry repository, its PEM CA bundle and digest, a private JSON credentials file, and the approved HTTPS token and blob origins; publish calls appbuild.PublishImage, which pushes over TLS and reads the image back; retrieve also takes the signature flags of signatureFlags, refuses --image and a missing signature flag by name, and calls appbuild.RetrieveImage (ST-BLD-QRY04-H) with the signature check. verify and export (ST-BLD-CLI11) read the image record, the OCI image folder, the build record and a work folder; verify also takes the signature flags, refuses a missing one by name, and calls appbuild.VerifyImage with the signature check; export calls appbuild.ExportImage.

title: main.runImageSign
description: runImageSign parses stego image sign (ST-BLD-CLI05) with the flag package: --image, --record-sha256 and the signature flags that signatureFlags adds, which image verify and image retrieve share. It refuses a missing flag by name, builds an appbuild.SignatureCheck with an appbuild.GitHubAttestationVerifier, calls appbuild.SignImage, and prints the image digest, the signer, the transparency log entry and each attestation.

title: main.main
description: main reads the first argument and calls the function that parses each command and its flags with the flag package: runInit for stego init (ST-DECL-CLI01), which requires --archetype and calls compiler.Initialize in the working folder; runValidate for stego validate (ST-DECL-CLI02), which calls compiler.Validate and prints compiler.FormatValidation; runVersion for stego version (ST-DIS-CLI07), which prints the version, or with --json encodes the version and buildidentity.Current as JSON; runFill for stego fill create (ST-EXT-CLI01), which resolves the registry, finds the component that owns the slot, reads the slot's proto contract, and writes fills/<name>/fill.yaml and fill.go; runTest for stego test (ST-EXT-CLI02), which parses a flag set with no flags, so a first argument that starts with - is refused unless it follows --, and runs go test ./fills/... with the remaining arguments; it records no evidence yet; runApply for stego apply (ST-GEN-CLI01), which calls compiler.Reconcile and compiler.Apply, and takes no flag yet: it has no flag to allow a hand edit, no flag to override a pin that does not stand, cannot read a saved plan, and writes no architecture view yet; runDrift for stego drift (ST-GEN-CLI06), which calls compiler.DetectDrift on out/; runPlan for stego plan, which makes a plan with compiler.Reconcile and prints compiler.FormatPlan (ST-GEN-CLI03) and gets the saved plan (ST-GEN-CLI03), though it saves and reads no plan yet; and runRegistry for stego registry fills (ST-SUP-CLI06), which reads fills/*/fill.yaml, stego registry inspect (ST-SUP-CLI02) and stego registry search (ST-SUP-CLI03), which load the resolved registry; search prints with a tabwriter, and inspect with fmt.Printf. runValidate, runPlan and runApply read the declaration (service.yaml) and the registry the project resolves, from the working folder; fill create and the registry search and inspect read the resolved registry; runInit writes service.yaml and reads none. The commands of the other cmd/stego files are dispatched from main too.

title: qualify-compiler-release.main
description: main parses the arguments of the release script with argparse: --revision, --output and --gh, all required, for qualify-compiler-release.py (ST-DIS-CLI03), and with --verify-release for qualify-compiler-release.py --verify-release (ST-DIS-CLI04). qualify refuses a revision that is not a full lower-case commit ID, a --gh that is not an absolute path to an executable GitHub CLI, and an output folder that exists. Through gh it reads the passed release decision attested at the commit, the CI runs at the commit (the compiler checks run and the signed artifact run), their jobs and artifacts, and the signatures. With --verify-release it also installs the published release through install-compiler.py, as a consumer does, checks that the compiler-<revision> tag points at the commit, and cross-checks the asset digests, the release notes and the signing run. It writes qualification.json into the new output folder, prints the same JSON, and exits with the reason on a CheckError, SIGINT or SIGTERM.

title: install-compiler.main
description: main parses the arguments of the installation script with argparse: --revision, --output and --gh, all required, and one of --release or --package, for install-compiler.py (ST-DIS-CLI05). install refuses a revision that is not a full lower-case commit ID, a host that is not Linux amd64, a --gh that is not an absolute path to an executable GitHub CLI, and an output folder that exists. With --release it downloads the compiler-<revision> release record and its fixed asset set through gh by asset ID into a temporary folder and checks each size and digest; with --package it reads the assets from that folder. verify-compiler-artifact.py then checks both signatures against the fixed source and signer policy and puts the binary and build.json in the output folder. It prints the verified record as JSON.
